extra.message: Cross-cohort privilege escalation in discussion_moderate — instructor can moderate threads belonging to a different cohort

metadata.proof: The moderation check at line 547 verifies the instructor is assigned to ANY cohort of the course (thread.course.cohorts.filter(instructors=...)), but DiscussionThread has a nullable cohort field (thread.cohort) that scopes a thread to a specific cohort. An instructor assigned only to Cohort A of Course X can moderate a thread belonging to Cohort B of Course X because the check is course-level rather than cohort-level. The correct check would be: if thread.cohort, validate assignment to thread.cohort.instructors.

extra.message: Unrestricted file upload via Resource.objects.create() bypassing FileExtensionValidator — any file type can be uploaded

metadata.citation:
resource = Resource.objects.create(
            title=title,
            file=file,
            category=category,
            uploader=request.user,
        )
metadata.proof: The file_upload view (line 835) creates a Resource instance via Resource.objects.create() without using a ModelForm. Django's Model.objects.create() does NOT call full_clean(), so the FileExtensionValidator defined on the Resource.file field (models.py line 155) is NEVER invoked. An attacker can upload any file type — executables, scripts, webshells — regardless of extension. The file is stored under MEDIA_ROOT/uploads/{user_id}/{uuid}{ext} and served via file_download. The only gate is @login_required.

extra.message: API keys stored in plaintext in the database

metadata.proof: The ApiKey model's `key` field (line 370) stores the full API key value as a plain CharField with no hashing. In the api_keys view (line 889), `key.key = uuid.uuid4().hex` generates the raw key and saves it directly to the database. The keys are also returned to authenticated users via the api_keys view and template. If the database is compromised, all API keys are immediately readable. Standard practice is to hash API keys (e.g., SHA-256) on creation, store only the hash, and display the raw key once.

extra.message: API keys have no expiry mechanism

metadata.citation:
class ApiKey(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="api_keys")
    name = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    key = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    last_used_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
metadata.proof: The ApiKey model has no `expires_at` field. Once created, an API key is valid indefinitely unless an admin manually sets `is_active=False`. There is no rotation policy, no maximum lifetime, and no automatic expiry. A leaked key that goes undetected grants permanent access. Standard practice requires API keys to have a configurable TTL with automatic expiration.

extra.message: Account deactivation via admin_user_edit is ineffective — form sets custom is_active_account but does not sync Django's is_active

metadata.proof: The UserManageForm (forms.py line 126) includes the custom field `is_active_account` (line 128) but NOT Django's built-in `is_active` field. When a school admin uses the edit form (admin_user_edit lines 585-587) to set `is_active_account=False`, `form.save()` writes only the custom field. Django's authentication backend checks `user.is_active`, not `user.is_active_account`, so the user can still log in. Compare with admin_user_toggle (lines 605-606) which correctly syncs both: `user.is_active = user.is_active_account`. The application never checks `is_active_account` in any authorization gate.

extra.message: Password change does not invalidate existing API keys

metadata.proof: The change_password view (line 108-115) uses Django's PasswordChangeForm and calls update_session_auth_hash to preserve the current session, but does NOT revoke, rotate, or deactivate the user's existing API keys. An API key issued before a password change remains fully valid afterward. If credentials were compromised and the user changes their password thinking all access is revoked, the API key still grants access. The view should call ApiKey.objects.filter(user=request.user, is_active=True).update(is_active=False) or similar.

extra.message: Unbounded query in admin_audit_log — all audit log records loaded with no pagination

While the view is restricted to school_admin, a malicious or compromised admin account could trigger excessive memory consumption by allowing the audit log to grow unbounded. The rendered template iterates the entire queryset.

extra.message: Mass assignment of assignment status bypasses workflow transitions

metadata.proof: The AssignmentForm allowslist includes `status` (line 54). When creating or editing an assignment via assignment_create (line 442) or assignment_edit (line 455), an instructor can set any status value (draft, published, closed, archived) directly from the POST body. This bypasses the status transition logic enforced only by the assignment_status view (line 467), which validates against `valid_transitions`. An instructor could jump from 'draft' directly to 'published' or from 'closed' to 'archived' without the intended workflow gate.
